summary.text: Dan Livingston ran for New York State Assembly District 123 and lost the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary to Dan Norton, 40.0 percent to 59.8 percent; Ballotpedia says he will not appear on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.

paragraphs.text: According to his Ballotpedia survey answers, Livingston first came to Binghamton as a student at Binghamton University and later returned to the area, where he served a term of service with AmeriCorps at the Broome County Council of Churches.
He said he volunteered for Bernie Sanders's 2016 presidential campaign, won a race for Binghamton's 2nd District in 2018, and served on the city council the following year.
He said he was a delegate to the Democratic National Convention for Sanders in 2020 and from 2021 to 2023 was the founding executive director of the Cannabis Association of New York.
In the survey, Livingston listed his campaign's key messages as taxing the rich, dignity for immigrants and clean water for all, and said he was most passionate about technology policy.
He listed endorsements from the Working Families Party of New York, Citizen Action of New York and the Civil Service Employees Association.
